vos.title: Eric Balchunas Sees Bitcoin (BTC) ETF Assets Tripling Gold at $300-400 Billion
vos.subTitle:
• Eric Balchunas predicts Bitcoin (BTC) ETF assets could reach $300-400 billion, tripling the gold ETF market.
• Balchunas doubled down Friday on X after a user questioned whether tripling gold was too aggressive.
• Three drivers cited: a younger investor base, growing institutional adoption, and stronger marketing firepower.
A $300-400 Billion AUM Scenario
Eric Balchunas, the senior ETF analyst at Bloomberg, expects spot Bitcoin ETFs to eventually grow to three times the size of the gold ETF market — a scenario that would lift Bitcoin (BTC) fund assets under management to between $300 billion and $400 billion. Balchunas first laid out the forecast in a recent interview, and when an X user pushed back on whether tripling gold was too aggressive, he doubled down on Friday. “BTC ETFs assets triple gold ETFs assets. That would mean BTC AUM hits $300-400b. Totally realistic long term imo,” he wrote in the reply. The projection is framed as a long-term trajectory rather than a near-term target; if it lands, the Bitcoin fund complex would rank among the largest commodity-linked ETF categories in existence.
Three forces underpin the thesis. The first is demographic: Bitcoin’s investor base is far younger than gold’s, and Balchunas argues that as younger generations accumulate wealth they will default to the asset they grew up with as their store of value. “I think as the younger investors get more money and grow up with Bitcoin as their quote-unquote store of value, I do believe the Bitcoin ETFs will triple gold in assets,” he said. The second is institutional adoption: he expects major financial institutions to lean harder on the asset in portfolios if its volatility continues to decline and its correlation with technology stocks weakens. The third is raw momentum — in his words, there is “way more enthusiasm and sales firepower” behind Bitcoin than gold products have ever commanded. The thesis effectively assumes that generations raised on HODL culture will come to control the bulk of investable wealth — a transfer of conviction, not merely of capital, one we track in our Bitcoin coverage.
Gold’s 5,000-Year Head Start
Balchunas is equally candid about why gold still owns the institutional room today. “Bitcoin is like gold as a teenager,” he said — gold is roughly 5,000 years old and “was mentioned 450 times in the Bible,” while Bitcoin is a 17-year-old asset. For conservative capital, that gap in history is not cosmetic: gold’s price swings are substantially milder, and millennia of monetary track record anchor its credibility with pension funds, insurers and sovereign desks. It is a credibility race measured in centuries, and Bitcoin is new to it. Volatility is also the objection Balchunas encounters most often — in surveys run by ETF issuers, institutional investors consistently cite price swings as their chief reservation about Bitcoin. He framed Bitcoin’s current stage of development as adolescence: technically functional, but still proving itself to risk-averse allocators. That framing matters because it isolates the exact variable institutions are pricing — not Bitcoin’s design or its custody rails, but its day-to-day behavior. Balchunas treats the hesitation as time-limited: if volatility keeps compressing and market structure matures, he anticipates an “inflection moment” at which large institutions begin treating Bitcoin as a dependable store of value or a portfolio diversifier. The access layer is already widening in parallel — EU banks widening Bitcoin access as the MiCA registry doubled to 80 — and issuers themselves are investing in the asset’s durability, with VanEck’s Sigel pointing to BIP-360 as a quantum-risk defense.
From Adolescence to Inflection
COINOTAG’s read: the weight of Balchunas’s call sits less in the $300-400 billion figure than in the condition his own X post — the primary record of the forecast — attaches to it: adoption, not price. Institutional participation is already compounding through treasury-style structures such as the strategic Bitcoin reserve model. Whether the tripling happens will therefore be read as a referendum on market maturity, not on marketing. Live market data shows Bitcoin spot moved 6.0% over the past 24 hours — a reminder that the very variable he flags as the gate, volatility, remains front and center.

vos.title: The Fed Hiked, Bitcoin Held Is Crypto Becoming Harder to Shake?
vos.subTitle:
For years, crypto traders have been trained to fear two words:

Rate hike.

Higher interest rates usually make life harder for risk assets. Money becomes more expensive, government bonds become more attractive, and speculative markets can lose liquidity.

So when the Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points on September 16, taking its target range to 3.75%–4.00%, another sharp Bitcoin sell-off would not have been surprising. It was the Fed's first increase since 2023.

But Bitcoin didn't collapse.

Instead, BTC absorbed the announcement and remained around $76,000 the following day.

That raises an interesting question.

Is crypto becoming harder to shake?

Bitcoin Knew the Hike Was Coming

The first explanation is probably the simplest.

The rate increase wasn't a major surprise.

Before the decision, markets had already assigned a very high probability to a 25-basis-point hike. In other words, traders had days to adjust their positions before the Fed actually announced anything.

Markets don't simply react to good or bad news.

They react to surprises.

If everyone expects bad news and prepares for it beforehand, the actual announcement can sometimes produce a surprisingly small reaction.

That appears to be part of what happened with Bitcoin.

The Fed hiked.

BTC moved around.

But there was no immediate macro-driven collapse.

Bitcoin Had Already Been Tested

The Fed wasn't Bitcoin's first problem this month.

BTC had already fallen roughly 4% after the U.S. Senate failed to advance major crypto legislation earlier in the week.

Before that, traders were dealing with persistent inflation, high Treasury yields and expectations that tighter monetary policy was returning.

Bitcoin had also experienced a much larger decline before September.

After trading above $126,000 in October 2025, BTC fell toward $60,000 in late August 2026 before recovering above $70,000.

That context matters.

The market entering the Fed meeting was very different from one sitting at fresh highs with extreme optimism.

A lot of fear and selling had already happened.

Buyers Are Still Showing Up

Another important change is the structure of Bitcoin demand.

Bitcoin is no longer driven only by crypto-native traders.

Spot ETFs have created another channel through which traditional investors can gain exposure to BTC.

That doesn't guarantee permanent buying. ETF flows can move in both directions.

In fact, U.S. Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $450 million of net outflows on September 15 as BTC weakened around the failed crypto legislation vote.

But zoom out slightly and the picture becomes more complicated.

Reuters reported that Bitcoin ETFs attracted nearly $2 billion during the week of August 17 after eight consecutive weeks of outflows during May and June.

That tells us demand isn't simply disappearing.

It's moving with sentiment.

The Market Is Learning to Separate News From Price

This may be one of the most important developments.

A negative headline does not automatically equal a negative market reaction.

The Fed can hike rates while Bitcoin holds.

Regulatory legislation can suffer a setback while buyers eventually return.

Inflation can remain elevated while individual altcoins still outperform.

Zcash offered an extreme example after the Fed decision. ZEC jumped roughly 23% while Bitcoin gained less than 1%, with SOL, BNB and several other large cryptocurrencies also advancing.

That doesn't mean macro conditions no longer matter.

It means crypto is reacting to multiple forces at once.

Liquidity matters.

Institutional demand matters.

Regulation matters.

Narratives matter.

Positioning matters.

And expectations matter.

But One Fed Meeting Doesn't Prove Bitcoin Is Invincible

This is where traders need to be careful.

Bitcoin surviving one expected rate hike doesn't mean monetary policy has stopped affecting crypto.

The Fed itself says inflation remains elevated. Its latest projections put 2026 PCE inflation at 3.7% and core PCE inflation at 3.4%, both still above its 2% objective.

More importantly, the Fed isn't necessarily finished.

Sixteen of 18 policymakers projected at least one additional rate increase before the end of 2026.

The September hike may have been easy for markets to absorb because it was widely expected.

An unexpected change in inflation or monetary policy could produce a very different reaction.

Watch the Bond Market

There is another market crypto traders shouldn't ignore.

Treasuries.

Higher bond yields increase the return investors can earn from relatively lower-risk assets. That creates competition for capital that might otherwise move into Bitcoin, stocks or other risk assets.

Before the Fed meeting, long-term Treasury yields were approaching 5%, creating another potential obstacle for Bitcoin's recovery.

After the decision, Treasury yields initially rose alongside the dollar before easing somewhat on September 17.

If yields continue climbing, Bitcoin's resilience could face another test.

If yields cool, some of that pressure could ease.

This is why watching BTC alone doesn't tell the entire story.

Stability Could Open the Door for Altcoins

There is another interesting consequence if Bitcoin continues holding.

Capital may start looking elsewhere.

We are already seeing hints of selective rotation.

ZEC's 23% move is one example. Solana, BNB and HYPE also outperformed BTC following the Fed decision.

That doesn't confirm altseason.

But a stable Bitcoin can sometimes create a better environment for altcoins than a Bitcoin that is violently pumping or crashing.

When BTC becomes quieter, traders start searching for movement elsewhere.

That's when individual narratives can suddenly take control.

So Is Crypto Really Becoming Harder to Shake?

Maybe — but we need more evidence.

Bitcoin absorbing an expected Fed hike is a sign of resilience, not proof that BTC has become immune to macro pressure.

The stronger test would be what happens when the market receives something it hasn't already priced in.

A surprise inflation reading.

An unexpected change in Fed policy.

A sharp move in Treasury yields.

A major liquidity shock.

Those events would tell us much more about how durable Bitcoin's current strength really is.

For now, though, September has delivered an interesting message.

The Fed tightened.

The dollar jumped.

Treasury yields reacted.

Bitcoin stayed near $76,000.

Crypto hasn't become impossible to shake.

But shaking it may be getting harder than many traders expected.

vos.title: XRP (XRP) Rallies 8.6% to Reclaim $1.40 After Senate Blocks CLARITY Act
vos.subTitle:
• XRP gained 8.57% in 24 hours to trade at $1.4060, per COINOTAG data.
• The Senate cloture vote on the CLARITY Act failed 50-49 on September 15.
• 30-day whale inflows to Binance reached about 1.6 billion XRP, the highest since March 2026.
XRP Erases CLARITY-Vote Losses
XRP (XRP) has clawed back its losses from a bruising regulatory week, gaining roughly 7% in 24 hours to trade near $1.39 after briefly bottoming around $1.27. The rout began on September 15, when the Senate's procedural cloture vote on the CLARITY Act — the bill meant to establish a federal framework for digital assets — failed 50-49, well short of the 60 votes required to advance. The token slid more than 8% immediately afterward, and pressure intensified the next day as the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a 3.75%-4.00% range, a headwind for high-risk assets. Still, the selloff proved temporary. The broader market rallied in tandem — Bitcoin near $80,752 and Ethereum around $2,595 — as capital rotated into altcoins, and roughly $3.9 billion of XRP changed hands in a day, close to the 30-day average, a sign of genuine participation. For a deeper dive, see our XRP coverage.
Binance Whale Inflows Hit Six-Month High
On-chain data shows large holders have been moving XRP to Binance at the fastest pace in six months: 30-day whale inflows reached roughly 1.6 billion XRP, the highest reading since March 2026. Exchange inflows are typically watched as potential sell pressure, since tokens moved off personal wallets are easier to sell — but a transfer is not a sale, and market-making, collateral and liquidity management all drive such flows. On September 11, daily inflows of 91.23 million XRP were actually offset by 113.91 million XRP in outflows, underscoring why net flow matters more than gross deposits. Notably, XRP held the $1.30 area even as inflows climbed, suggesting buyers are absorbing the supply. Exchange-side reshuffles tell a similar story: Uphold moving 500 million XRP worth $649 million across five new wallets was custody restructuring, not distribution. More on the same theme in our whales report.
XRPL Payments Double Monthly Average
Network activity on the XRP Ledger, the layer-1 protocol behind the token, surged alongside the price recovery. Daily payment volume exceeded 1.1 billion XRP over the past 24 hours, more than double the 30-day average of roughly 494.6 million XRP. Total transactions rose 23.9% to 2.2 million, successful transactions climbed 11.2% to about 1.5 million, and active accounts jumped 21.5% to 18,700. There is a nuance, though: active users fell 17.3% to around 155,300, implying much of the jump reflects larger or more frequent transfers from existing participants rather than broad new adoption. The activity spike coincides with XRP's recovery from its correction after an August run that approached $1.70, and infrastructure metrics have stayed resilient in parallel — Ripple CTO David Schwartz recently noted that Ledger hub peers climbed back to 501.
Golden Cross Comes Into View
The technical picture is quietly improving. XRP opened the day at $1.2964, pushed as high as $1.4028 and settled near $1.3863 — a 6.93% daily gain and one of its sharpest single-day moves in weeks. Beneath the surface, the gap between the 50-day and 200-day exponential moving averages has narrowed to its tightest point since August 2024, the setup that precedes a golden cross; at the current pace, that crossover could form on the daily chart as soon as mid-October. One caution flag: the 4-hour chart already flipped bullish on August 21, but the gap there has been closing rather than widening, so the daily confirmation is not a lock. The rest of the board looks healthier — ADX sits at 35.2 with DI+ above DI-, RSI is at a neutral 54.6, and the Squeeze Momentum indicator has fired for 11 straight bars, hinting at a compression before a larger move.
Structurally, the token remains inside a descending channel on the 4-hour timeframe, having rejected near $1.48 and dropped to the $1.25 zone before rebounding. The immediate test is the $1.33-$1.37 resistance band; a clean break and hold would target the channel's upper boundary around $1.40-$1.45, while a rejection risks a return to $1.25. Deeper dynamic supports sit at the 200-day moving average near $1.30 and the 100-day average around $1.18. On the upside, the $1.60-$1.70 swing-high zone guards the path to $1.90. Some chartists are also tracking an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern on the daily chart, watching a neckline near $1.55 that, if confirmed, could open the way toward $2. Investors weighing an entry can review our guide on where to buy XRP.
$1.4255 Resistance in Focus
COINOTAG's proprietary 42-indicator composite S/R scoring engine frames the immediate battleground: XRP trades at $1.4060, up 8.57% in 24 hours, and our composite engine rates the $1.4255 resistance at 84/100 (STRONG), driven by the confluence of the Value Area High, a high-volume node, the POC and the Bollinger upper band, with $1.5172 next at 80/100 on the Keltner upper and Fibonacci 0.236. On the downside, $1.3436 support scores 86/100 from the ATR lower band, Ichimoku Senkou A/B and Fibonacci 0.500. Derivatives positioning adds a caution: funding is mildly positive at 0.0066% with $960.5 million in open interest, but the 2.74 long/short ratio (73.2% long) signals crowded positioning, and the Fear & Greed Index at 56 (Greed) can feed FOMO-driven chasing. RSI at 56.10 leaves room, though MACD is still bearish and the trend sideways. A daily close above $1.4255 would open $1.5172; losing $1.3436 invalidates the bullish thesis.

vos.title: Fake AI Trading Bot Tutorials Drain 274.6 Ethereum (ETH) From 224 Victims, TRM Labs Finds
vos.subTitle:
• Fake YouTube tutorials promoting Claude AI arbitrage bots drained 274.6 ETH
• TRM Labs traced 234 malicious contracts deployed by 224 victims
• Stolen funds worth about $517,000 moved to six collection addresses
274.6 ETH Lost to Fake Claude Tutorials
A network of fake YouTube tutorials promising an automated arbitrage bot built with Anthropic’s Claude has drained 274.6 Ethereum (ETH), worth roughly $517,000, from 224 victims, according to a Sep. 14 report from blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. The operation stood out from conventional drainer campaigns because it never asked anyone to connect a wallet to a suspicious site or sign an unclear approval. Instead, victims followed step-by-step video instructions and deployed malicious smart contracts themselves, executing every transaction with their own approvals. TRM identified nine near-identical tutorials circulated under different creator identities, each fronted by AI-generated hosts and voiceovers that lent the videos the look of independent guides. Viewers were told to copy code and open a compiler website chosen by the presenter, some of which copied the design of Remix, the widely used browser-based environment for building Ethereum contracts. The firm traced 234 contracts deployed through the funnel; because several participants created more than one, the affected headcount came to 224. Once funded, the contracts forwarded balances to six collection addresses controlled by the operators, and TRM calculated a median loss of 1 ETH per incident — evidence that the take was distributed across many small victims rather than concentrated in one large deposit. Based on ETH’s price when the transfers settled, the aggregate haul reached approximately $517,000.
How the Hidden Drainer Code Worked
The deception sat one layer earlier than most phishing: at code generation. In the variant TRM examined, a backend script ignored whatever source the victim pasted into the compiler and instead retrieved a separate contract from a server the scammers controlled, preparing the replacement for deployment. The clean code displayed in the browser never reached the chain — users saw one program on screen while their wallets deployed another, so a visual check of the compiler window could not reveal the swap. The replacement contract accepted ETH deposits, matching the expected behavior of a trading bot that needed working capital. But once its balance exceeded 0.05 ETH, the contract was set to sweep the money to an operator-controlled address the moment the user pressed either the Start or Withdraw button. Both controls served the same drain function despite their legitimate-looking labels, and no AI model ever interacted with the deployed code — the Claude branding was purely part of the pitch. Because each victim initiated and approved the deployment, funding and function calls — paying their own gas fees at every step — the transaction trail looked nothing like a typical attack requesting a broad token allowance. Common wallet protections had little to flag: a fresh contract address would not appear on existing blocklists, and no seed phrase was ever surrendered.
Bytecode Verification Becomes the First Defense
Our reading of this campaign is that the attack surface has shifted from wallet approvals to the code-supply chain itself, and users deploying anything from a tutorial should verify the actual bytecode before funding it. Context matters: Ethereum security groups, including the Ethereum ecosystem’s Security Alliance network spanning MetaMask, Phantom, WalletConnect and Backpack, put 2025 drainer losses at $84 million — the lowest on record — and the Ethereum Foundation backed a dedicated engineer in February to disrupt such tooling. As tutorials grow more convincing, that downward trend faces a real test.

vos.title: "Micron Rebounds 5.5% as Memory Tightness Returns to Focus, Taiwan Labor Talks Hit Key Date"
vos.subTitle:
Micron Technology shares jumped 5.5% to $977.50 on Thursday, putting the stock back above its pre-Monday level as tight memory supply returned to the center of the semiconductor trade.
The rebound now meets a company-specific labor test in Taiwan, where Friday is one of two key mediation dates, and unions have warned they could move toward a strike vote if Micron fails to produce a concrete profit-sharing proposal.
Micron Erases Monday’s AI-Slowdown Selloff
Micron fell 5.25% to $924.03 on Monday as calls from several AI-industry leaders for slower AI development pressured chipmakers. By Thursday’s close, the stock had climbed back to $977.50, about 0.2% above its Sept. 11 close of $975.26, effectively erasing the net loss from the week’s initial AI-slowdown shock, according to Micron’s historical closing prices. Reuters reported that the Monday decline came as AI-slowdown warnings broadly hit semiconductor shares.
Thursday’s move was not isolated. Intel gained 7.7%, AMD rose about 6.5%, and SanDisk advanced 6.2% during a broad semiconductor rebound, while falling oil prices and Treasury yields also supported the wider market. Micron also had a memory-specific tailwind after Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan warned that memory capacity remained constrained and supply pressure could persist into next year.
That supply backdrop matters because Micron’s recent earnings have been built on unusually strong memory pricing and margins. Micron’s fiscal third-quarter results showed revenue of $41.46 billion and a non-GAAP gross margin of 84.9%, followed by guidance for roughly $50 billion of fourth-quarter revenue and an approximately 86% gross margin.
Wall Street is also focused on how long the memory shortage can last. Goldman Sachs maintained a “Neutral” rating and $1,100 target on Sept. 11, expecting another strong quarter because of tight DRAM and NAND conditions while flagging longer-term supply additions, particularly from China. TD Cowen’s Krish Sankar, by contrast, reiterated a “Buy” rating and $1,600 target this week, arguing that Micron appears further along in margin expansion than in the underlying demand cycle. 
Taiwan Labor Dispute Puts Supply Risk Back in Focus
The same tight-supply story that helped Micron shares Thursday increases the significance of its Taiwan labor dispute. According to Reuters’ report on Micron’s Taiwan labor dispute, unions representing more than 80% of Micron’s roughly 15,000 Taiwan employees are seeking a permanent system allocating 15% of operating profit to employees. Union representatives said that if Micron does not present a concrete proposal during the Sept. 18 and Sept. 21 process, they could declare negotiations broken down and move toward a strike vote.
No strike had been called, and production had not been affected in Reuters’ latest confirmed report. Friday marks the Taichung union’s scheduled first mediation session, while further mediation involving the Taoyuan union is scheduled for Sept. 21. A Friday-morning status review found no confirmed strike announcement or production interruption.
Taiwan is nevertheless a critical Micron manufacturing center for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory, meaning an eventual work stoppage could matter more while memory supply is already constrained. Micron has said it remains committed to participating in mediation in good faith.
The dispute continued even after Micron announced fiscal-2026 rewards worth 35 to 68 months of pay for Taiwan direct labor employees. The union has argued that those awards are one-off compensation rather than the permanent, transparent profit-sharing structure it is seeking. Reuters detailed Micron’s Taiwan compensation package.
Tokenized Micron Market Remains Active
Separately, Micron’s tokenized counterpart remains active on Binance. Binance officially opened MUB/USDT Spot trading in June, establishing MUB as an active bStock linked to Micron.
At the latest check on Friday morning, Binance’s MUB/USDT Spot market showed MUB at $992.49.
MUB trades in a different market and measurement window from Micron’s Thursday 5.5% regular-session gain, so the figures should not be treated as directly equivalent. Binance states that MUB is a bStock issued by BTech Holdings representing an interest in underlying securities rather than direct ownership of Micron shares.
Micron’s next confirmed financial catalyst comes Sept. 30, when the company will hold its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call at 2:30 p.m. Mountain time. Micron confirmed the Sept. 30 earnings date in August.
Investor Takeaway
Micron’s 5.5% Thursday rally restored the stock to roughly its pre-Monday level as attention swung back from AI-spending concerns toward memory scarcity. The Taiwan dispute now tests that supply narrative from another direction, with the Sept. 18 and Sept. 21 mediation process preceding any potential strike vote and Micron’s Sept. 30 earnings providing the next confirmed financial update.

vos.title: Binance Withdraws Greek MiCA License Bid for Bitcoin (BTC) Services After Lagarde Intervention
vos.subTitle:
• Binance withdrew its Greek MiCA license application on June 24, before any formal decision was issued
• ECB President Christine Lagarde reportedly asked Greek PM Mitsotakis to block Binance's approval
• Greece's capital market commission had notified ESMA of its intent to approve Binance's application
Binance Pulls Greek Application June 24
Binance has withdrawn its application for a Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) license in Greece after European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde privately intervened to block its approval, according to a report published Sept. 18 by The Wall Street Journal. Lagarde is said to have personally asked Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis not to green-light the filing — a request that preceded Binance's decision to pull the application on June 24. The license would have allowed Binance to offer regulated crypto-asset services, including trading and custody of assets such as Bitcoin (BTC), across the entire bloc. As of the report's publication, neither Lagarde, the ECB nor the Greek authorities involved had confirmed or denied the account, and Binance has made no public statement addressing the reported intervention.
The application had been moving toward approval. The Hellenic Capital Market Commission, the national regulator reviewing the file, had determined that Binance's documentation was complete and, following MiCA procedure, notified the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) of its intent to approve. The turn came in early June, when the commission informed Binance that Lagarde had voiced her opposition directly to the Greek prime minister. Binance then withdrew on June 24, which meant the commission's board never had to issue a formal rejection. The only objectively verifiable fact remains the withdrawal itself — Binance holds no MiCA license from any EU member state. The report attributed two concerns to Lagarde: Binance's guilty-plea record in the United States, and the expansion of dollar-denominated stablecoins, whose tokenomics could undercut the ECB's digital euro project and euro-denominated alternatives. What makes the episode notable is jurisdiction. Under ESMA's MiCA framework, licensing authority sits with each member state's national regulator, and a license granted in any single state passports the holder EU-wide — the ECB holds no formal approval or veto role. What the reporting describes, then, is not a central bank exercising statutory power but its president working through political channels to influence a member-state government.
Banks Double on ESMA Register
As one crypto-native incumbent exits the EU's licensing track, traditional banks are racing onto the same register. The number of banks listed as crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) under MiCA doubled to about 80 from roughly 40 between June 26 and Sept. 16, based on ESMA's official register data. Over the same period, the total count of listed CASPs climbed from 243 to 349 — but non-bank providers lost relative ground, their share slipping from about 84% to 77%, while banks lifted theirs from around 17% to nearly 23%. The profile of Europe's regulated crypto market is visibly shifting toward incumbent finance.
Germany accounts for much of the banking influx. Dozens of cooperative and commercial lenders appear on the register, including institutions from the Volksbank, Raiffeisenbank and VR Bank networks — evidence that regulated crypto services are reaching regional banking, not just global groups. Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest lender, announced plans on Wednesday to launch digital asset custody for institutional and corporate clients in Europe, with a spokesperson indicating the bank expects MiCA regulatory approval for the offering in October. Institutional custody of this kind is a different proposition from the self-custody model retail users manage with hardware devices and a Ledger Recovery Key; banks are building the custodial rails that funds and corporates require. The speed of the expansion owes to a structural shortcut: where crypto companies must complete full CASP authorization, credit institutions can offer crypto-asset services — custody, trading and execution across spot and derivatives such as crypto options — through a lighter notification route. Article 60 of MiCA permits a credit institution to provide these services provided it submits the required information to its home regulator at least 40 working days before offering them for the first time. Lenders already distributing conventional instruments like the S&P 500 ETF can therefore enter crypto without a bespoke licensing process.
MiCA Passport Becomes the Prize
Taken together, the two threads sketch a European market at an inflection point. The register's own composition shows who is winning access: the framework ESMA administers is being absorbed fastest by incumbent banks using the Article 60 notification route, while the industry's most heavily used exchange was reportedly squeezed out through channels outside the rulebook. Our reading at COINOTAG is that the MiCA passport is now the decisive asset in Europe — and who obtains it is being settled as much by politics as by the authorization files themselves.

vos.title: EU Banks on MiCA Registry Double to 80, Widening Bitcoin (BTC) Access
vos.subTitle:
• Banks on the EU MiCA CASP registry doubled from about 40 to 80 by September 16.
• Total authorized CASPs grew from 243 to 349 over the same period.
• Bank share of the CASP register rose from 17% to 23%.
From 40 Banks to 80
The register of firms authorized to serve Europe's crypto market under MiCA used to read almost entirely like a startup directory — specialist brokers, custodians and trading venues built for digital assets from day one. That composition is shifting toward institutions, and the shift is now measurable. Registry data shows the number of banks listed as crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets framework doubled from roughly 40 to 80 between June 26 and September 16, according to Coinreaders. Over the same window, the total count of authorized CASPs climbed from 243 to 349, which means new bank entrants took a disproportionate slice of every registration added across the summer. The share math makes the tilt explicit: banks held 17% of the register in late June and 23% by mid-September, while non-bank providers — the firms that defined the first phase of Europe's licensed market — slipped from roughly 84% to 77%. All figures reflect the September 16 snapshot of the register. A CASP authorization is the umbrella license MiCA created for custody, exchange operation, execution and advice: a firm that secures it in one member state can passport those services across the entire bloc. The dynamic tracks the framework's maturation rather than a single quarter's anomaly. As MiCA's authorization regime settles into routine operation, the onboarding queue is no longer dominated by crypto-native applicants racing the compliance deadline. Licensed banks that spent the framework's early months observing from the sidelines are filing in steadily increasing numbers, and each approval converts a traditional institution into a regulated gateway for Bitcoin (BTC) and the wider token market inside the European Union. For a framework whose early skeptics doubted legacy finance would bother applying at all, the register now supplies a clear empirical answer: the banks are applying, the pace is accelerating, and the institutional share of Europe's licensed crypto infrastructure rises with every reporting cycle.
What a CASP License Buys a Bank
The June-to-September window captures MiCA's first full quarter of steady-state operation, which is what makes the doubling of bank registrations more than a bookkeeping curiosity. For the institutions, the filing calculus is straightforward: a CASP license obtained from one national competent authority unlocks a passport across all 27 member states, letting a bank extend an existing deposit and brokerage relationship into digital assets without erecting a fresh legal entity per country. In practical terms, that means a retail client can be offered token custody, spot execution and — where the underlying networks permit — staking on proof-of-stake chains under the same regulated roof as familiar savings products. The competitive pressure lands on the specialist venues that built Europe's licensed retail market. Firms whose platforms were engineered around granular candlestick trading of tokens issued via smart contracts now compete with banks delivering equivalent regulated services inside apps customers already open every day — a distribution advantage the crypto-native sector spent years assembling along the Robinhood-style retail brokerage model. The framework's effect on established European trading venues is one of licensing-parity pressure rather than displacement: the specialists keep their head start, but the moat narrows with each bank approval, and the contrast sharpens when licensed local providers are set against the best crypto exchanges globally. What carries over untouched is scale. With 349 authorized CASPs as of September 16, non-bank firms still outnumber bank registrants roughly three to one and hold 77% of the register. The institutional acceleration widens the market's regulated perimeter; it has not yet rewritten its leadership. The direction, though, is unambiguous: every reporting window since late June has added banks to the list, the share arithmetic moved roughly six points in a single summer, and the reading around the data is uniform — with MiCA's regime in place, the pace of European banks' entry into crypto is picking up cycle by cycle.
The 77% Non-Bank Majority
The legal footing for all of it is Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 — MiCA itself — whose CASP title has bound every firm offering crypto-asset services in the Union since December 30, 2024, with the stablecoin provisions applying six months earlier. The rule text requires authorization from a home-state national competent authority before any such services may be offered; the doubling of bank entries is that requirement operating as designed, filtering applicants into a single, passportable license. What it does not change is who holds most of the register: with non-bank firms still at 77%, Europe's specialist crypto layer remains the majority — for now — even as the institutional share climbs.

vos.title: The One Distinction Between Spot and Futures That Keeps Traders Broke
vos.subTitle:
📉📈
89% of futures traders are liquidated in their first month. Here is what the 11% do differently. When I lost my initial $5,400, I thought I was trading crypto. In reality, I was gambling on price direction while being completely blind to the mechanics of leverage. Spot trading is simple ownership: you buy $BTC at $60,000, and even if it dips to $50,000, you still hold the same amount of coins. You wait for the market cycle. Futures, however, is a contract on the future price of an asset, and the mechanism that catches everyone off guard is the liquidation price. In spot, you can be wrong for months and survive.
